summary: `FORGE_FRAMING` requires the timestamp field, so every forge line framed without one keeps its whole `job\tstep\t` prefix — and a framed empty line survives the drop, spending the budget

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: a failing lane's rendered log carries no forge decoration on any line, and a line the forge framed around nothing costs no budget; the drain reads failing titles from the head of the log rather than trimming them away.
tests: the shed strips the forge's frame from a log line the job name frames without a timestamp
the shed drops a log line the forge framed around an empty message
notes: Lane-observed on run 35008214078: ~380 tail lines rendered as `windows\tRun pnpm test\t…`, many holding nothing but the prefix, while 1160 head lines — carrying three reds' titles — were trimmed. The job name is a fact the lane declared (`CiLane.job`), so the frame is read, not guessed (`engine-boundary.md`, *Told, not inferred*); a bare two-field strip would eat the leading columns of any tab-carrying test output.

edit.description: `plantForge` puts the stub's dir on a PATH the host's own forge CLI is not on, so the direct spawn reaches the stub or nothing

summary: `plantForge` prepends its dir but leaves the host's PATH behind it, so on a host whose real `gh` the direct spawn can reach, five cases read the forge instead of the stub
acceptance: every lane-reader case is answered by the planted stub on every host, and the vacuity pins on the stub's call count hold for the stub's own invocations rather than for a CLI the fixture never planted.
pins: every lane-reader case reads its planted forge stub, with the host's own forge CLI off PATH
notes: Lane-observed: the `refuses` case rendered the real `gh`'s GH_TOKEN message, and the other four saw `calls().length === 0`. On win32 the stub is a `.cmd`, which a direct spawn skips; the search then walks on to the host's `gh.exe` further down PATH. The helper's own doc comment already states the isolation this breaks, and the absent-CLI case already shows the shape — PATH stripped to a single dir, the launcher naming `process.execPath` absolutely.

edit.description: the two deep-nest fixtures build and run git through the namespaced join the cases themselves pin

summary: the three win32 total-path cases nest their tree with a bare `join` and then run git in it, so the fixture hits the very limit the case exists to prove the engine clears
acceptance: each long-path case builds its fixture through `namespacedJoin` and reaches the engine call it names on win32, so the lane's verdict on these three is the engine's and not the fixture's.
pins: jobRm finds and removes a job whose dir nests past win32's ~260-char limit
jobNew doesn't misread an existing chain.ts or seedDir as absent when configDir/seedDir nests past win32's ~260-char limit
readPending/readPendingTolerant/commitPendingUpdate don't misread an existing or writable pending.json as absent when pendingPath exceeds win32's ~260-char limit
notes: Lane-observed: all three failed `spawn git ENOENT`, which is win32 refusing a cwd past the limit rather than a missing git. The idiom is the one the section names and the cases already exercise on the engine side. `job new` pins `core.longpaths` repo-locally on win32; a fixture that inits its own repo wants the same.
